text:
Alex Iafallo is doing the quiet work on a Winnipeg team that has found its feet. After four straight losses around the turn of the month, the Jets have won six in a row, and Iafallo has played about 14 minutes a night through it. He has 8 points in 21 games, 3 of them on the power play.

The interesting split is between his own luck and his line's. Personally he is running hot: 4 goals on 2.91 expected goals, a 16.7% shooting rate against a league 13.4%. But with him on the ice at five on five, the Jets have scored 4.34 fewer goals than their chances deserved, and they are winning 52% of the expected goals while he is out there, about 6 points better than when he sits. That's a change from last season, when Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level and his team created little offense with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so watch what he does in the seconds after a turnover. If the on-ice finishing evens out, his assists should follow.
